Six products, anchored by the flagship: **The Robbery Meter**, **Outfield
Cannons**, **Ground Crew Range**, **Web Gem of the Game**, **Double-Play
Ballet**, and **Pop-Time Pipeline**.


The most electric moment in baseball — an outfielder running down a ball that
should have dropped — had no number on the scoreboard. This gives it one.

Three physically meaningful features, engineered from tracking:

| feature | meaning |
|---|---|
| `route_ft` | straight-line distance from where the fielder stood at contact to the ball |
| `hang_s` | time from contact to the catch or landing |
| `req_speed` | `route_ft / hang_s` — the speed he would have to sustain to arrive |

Route and hang are the physics; **their ratio is what separates a routine fly
from a highlight**.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-catch
#| eval: false
source("../R/R07_defense.R")

fit <- fit_catch_model(catches)     # glm(catch_made ~ route_ft + hang_s + req_speed)
catch_model_metrics(fit)
plot_catch_model(fit)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-catch
#| eval: false
from components import c07_defense as c07
model = c07.fit_catch_model(tabs["catches"])
c07.catch_model_metrics(model)
```

:::

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| opportunities | **7,058** |
| base catch rate | 0.850 |
| accuracy | **0.955** |
| AUC | **0.954** |
| Brier score | 0.038 |

![The catch probability model](../outputs/figures/fig_catch_probability_model.png)

The curve reads exactly as intuition demands: a 60-foot route is nearly
automatic with five seconds of hang time and close to a coin flip with three.

## Outs Above Expected

Summing `catch made − catch probability` over every chance gives each fielder
the outs they recorded **beyond what an average defender would have**, given the
same opportunities.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-oae
#| eval: false
scored <- score_catches(fit)
outs_above_expected(scored, lineups, min_opps = 12, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-oae
#| eval: false
c07.outs_above_expected(tabs["catches"], model, lu, top=10)
```

:::

| player | pos | opportunities | made | OAE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PHD-5994 | LF | 254 | 223 | **+8.75** |
| PHD-8619 | LF | 279 | 261 | +5.79 |
| PHD-8007 | CF | 70 | 68 | +4.64 |

![Outs Above Expected](../outputs/figures/fig_oae_leaderboard.png)

## Web Gem of the Game

Every completed catch carries a **Robbery Score** of
$100 \times (1 - P(\text{catch}))$. Sorting by it surfaces the night's most
improbable play automatically — no producer required.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-gem
#| eval: false
web_gem(scored, lineups, top = 5)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-gem
#| eval: false
c07.web_gem(tabs["catches"], model, lu, top=5)
```

:::

| player | pos | route | hang | catch prob | robbery score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ZGC-9675 | RF | 139.8 ft | 6.45 s | 0.165 | **83.5** |
| ARN-3382 | LF | 137.9 ft | 6.55 s | 0.214 | 78.6 |

![The season's best web gem](../outputs/figures/fig_webgem_hero.png)

## Outfield Cannons

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-cannons
#| eval: false
outfield_cannons(throws, lineups, min_throws = 3, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-cannons
#| eval: false
c07.outfield_cannons(tabs["throws"], lu, top=10)
```

:::

Hardest measured throw: **102 mph**. League average is 66.6 mph across 8,553
tracked throws, so the leaderboard is genuinely separating arms.

::: {.callout-note}
## A join bug worth recording

The fielder lookup joins `fielder_id` to a lineup column. The lineup table can
carry more than one row per play, and the first version of this join silently
returned two rows per fielding play — doubling every leaderboard built from it.
Both implementations now de-duplicate on `(game_string, play_per_game)` first.
:::

## Ground Crew Range

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-range
#| eval: false
ground_crew_range(catches, lineups, min_catches = 8, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-range
#| eval: false
c07.ground_crew_range(tabs["catches"], lu, top=10)
```

:::

| player | pos | avg route | top closing | catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| XOZ-5625 | CF | **83.0 ft** | 19.8 mph | 11 |
| QBR-1229 | CF | 77.7 ft | 17.8 mph | 12 |

## Double-Play Ballet

Pivot time — glove to release for the middle infielder on the turn.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-dp
#| eval: false
double_play_ballet("y1_d122_IOL_VAS", plays, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-dp
#| eval: false
c07.double_play_ballet(game, plays, top=10)
```

:::

## Pop-Time Pipeline

Catcher exchange time and throw velocity to second base, measured from the
event stream and the ball's flight.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-pop
#| eval: false
pop_time_pipeline("y1_d122_IOL_VAS", plays, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-pop
#| eval: false
c07.pop_time_pipeline(game, plays, top=10)
```

:::

Across the showcase game, transfers averaged **1.25 s** with throws up to
91 mph — the raw material for a "can he throw him out?" graphic.
